note: Published relative risks (RR) used as PRIORS when no observed city data has been fitted. beta_a = ln(RR) / a_ref, where a_ref is the model's anomaly driver at the published exposure. These are order-of-magnitude anchors, not fits. Edit or add entries, then run: python backend/calibrate_risk.py --anchors-only

anchors.source: Azhar et al. 2014, PLOS ONE 9(3):e91831 - all-cause mortality rate ratio in the peak heat week (19-25 May 2010), Ahmedabad; the paper reports 1.76 and 2.12 depending on the reference period, the lower is used
anchors.caveat: a_ref is taken from the single hottest reading of the episode (46.8 C) against Ahmedabad's May ERA5 normal, although the RR is a weekly average. That understates the slope, so the anchor errs conservative.

anchors.source: Multi-city study 'Impact of heatwaves on all-cause mortality in India' (ScienceDirect pii S0160412024000473) - pooled +33.2% (95% CI 18.6 to 49.8) mortality when mean temperature exceeded the 99th percentile for at least 5 consecutive days; observed in Ahmedabad, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Varanasi
anchors.caveat: Pooled across cities, not city-specific. a_ref = 0.5 (IMD Heat Wave onset) is an assumption: sustained >99th-percentile heat is treated as at least Heat Wave severity.

anchors.source: Summer temperature and all-cause mortality 2006-2015, Hyderabad (PMC8843295) - about +16% mean daily deaths at Tmax >= 40 C
anchors.reason: Exposure is an absolute temperature threshold, not a departure from the city's normal, so it cannot be mapped onto the model's anomaly scale from this data alone. Kept for reference.

not_calibrated.Mumbai: No city-specific published RR entered. The multi-city study found Mumbai among the weakest heat-mortality associations, so the pooled value is not applied. Add observed data or an anchor to calibrate.
not_calibrated.hosp: No published heat-admissions RR entered for any of the four cities. Hospitalization stays on the default until admissions data is added to observed.csv.

Ahmedabad.note: 3,118 all-cause deaths in May, mean of 2009 and 2011 (Azhar et al. 2014) divided by 31 days; May only, pre-2012 city limits

Hyderabad.note: mean daily all-cause deaths on summer days 2006-2015 (PMC8843295); population has grown since
